paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. God was RIGHT THERE in that city, and she still wouldn't listen. Zephaniah says she "heeded no voice" and "accepted no correction" (Zephaniah 3:2). I think that is the heart of the whole passage: the trouble wasn't that God was far away, it was that nobody wanted to hear Him.

Look at who got it wrong, too: princes, judges, prophets and priests, the very ones who were supposed to lead people toward God (Zephaniah 3:3-4). And yet "The LORD within her is righteous; He does no wrong" (Zephaniah 3:5). Every morning He showed up with His justice, and "the unjust know no shame." That tells me God's goodness never wavers, even when everybody around it does.

So what does that mean for you, baker? When correction comes, it's a gift, not an insult, because God said, "Surely you will fear Me and accept correction," and then they "rose early to corrupt all their deeds" (Zephaniah 3:7). That's why it's so serious: the LORD says He has decided to pour out His burning anger on the nations, because refusing correction doesn't stay small (Zephaniah 3:8). I'm not saying that to scare you, I'm saying it because I've been the worn-out stamper who needed fixing, so keep your ears open, keep your heart soft, and let Him shape you.
